terms.grammar: adjective; aequum est + accusative and infinitive, it is reasonable
evidence: Ter. Eun. 3.2.25: quae līberum scīre aequom est adulēscentem (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Imp. Pomp. 47: sīcut aequum est
terms.comment: First “level, even”; so fair, just, reasonable. Aequī bonīque facere is “to accept as fair, put up with” (Ter. Heaut. 4.5.40). More than is reasonable is plūs aequō (Hor. Ep. 2.2.215: pōtus largius aequō).

evidence: Cic. Off. 3.20: ratiōnī disciplīnaeque maximē cōnsentānea (Lewis & Short, s.v. cōnsentāneus)
terms.comment: Of an opinion or an argument rather than a person; cōnsentāneum est, “it stands to reason”.

phrases.english: having drunk more than is reasonable

phrases.latin: Aequum est tē quoque aliquid labōris suscipere.
phrases.english: It’s only fair that you take on some of the work too.

sources: Lewis & Short: aequus · Lewis & Short: consentaneus
